target_customer: Shippers, carriers and freight brokers in logistics that pay for AI agents to run operations
problem: Freight is moved through brokers who take fees; the company first matched shippers directly with carriers (as Zerobroker) and now sells autonomous AI workers for logistics tasks.
business_model: B2B SaaS and AI agent subscription for logistics

founders.name: Georgy Melkonyan
education: PhD in transportation engineering (institution not named)
founders.background_notes: YC page: over 15 years solving logistics problems for shippers and carriers.

technical_complexity.rationale: A freight marketplace is standard software; the AI agent product from 2024 relies on LLMs integrated with TMS and load boards.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with TMS platforms give some lock in but digital freight matching and AI agents are widely copied.

incumbents: Digital freight brokers and large brokerages
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Flexport invested in the 2023 seed.

market_need_then: Freight brokers charge fees and the freight market is large; the 2020 Arrive Logistics piece described new entrants challenging incumbent brokers, though its content was not read.

branding.domain_note: Now uses arnata.com; earlier company name was Zerobroker.

rebrands.why: Not stated in sources opened; the exact date is not given by the sources (a FundersClub page lists Arnata as fka Zerobroker Technologies)

brand_strength.rationale: Previous name Zerobroker was a descriptive, adversarial label; the rename to Arnata is recent with no brand press found.

pivots.from: Zerobroker, broker free freight marketplace connecting shippers and carriers
pivots.to: Arnata, autonomous AI workers for logistics operations
pivots.why: Not stated in sources opened; dates not given

outcome_analysis: Arnata, formerly Zerobroker, raised a 6.5 million dollar seed in September 2023 with Flexport among investors and later rebranded to sell AI agents to logistics firms. No later round or exit was found, and the team stood at 15 people. The pivot from marketplace to AI agents suggests the original broker free model needed a new angle, but sources do not say why.
notes: Seed reported by FreightCaviar, VentureBeat and Signalbase via search results (VentureBeat was not opened because of fetch limits). Dealroom's 125K seed figure conflicts and is not used. Founding year conflicts (2017 on Dealroom and CB Insights, 2021 on Seedtable). Competitor search found no sources dated near 2021 naming rivals (Convoy, Uber Freight and others were not tied to Zerobroker in any source), so the list is empty.
